biography.plain_text: Panos J. Marinopoulos was a Greek businessman from the third generation of the Marinopoulos retail family. Born in Athens, he ran the Niki supermarket business and shared ownership of the family group behind Carrefour-Marinopoulos. His interests also extended to publishing through a stake in Petros Kostopoulos's Greek magazine company, IMAKO.

long_biography.plain_text:
Bringing Starbucks to Greece was a personal project for retailer Panos J. Marinopoulos. He secured the partnership with the American company, and the two groups announced their Greek joint venture in 2002. The arrangement paired Starbucks' coffee business with his family's experience of operating international brands in the local market.

The partnership expanded into Cyprus, where Marinopoulos served as president of the coffee company when its first Nicosia store opened. Coffee remained a business interest after the collapse of the family's supermarket group. The Greek company renewed its Starbucks franchise agreement for ten years in 2023.

uncertainties: Research began 30 September 2026; final source checks took place 1 October 2026, with no source later than the assigned 30 September cutoff used. Wealth relationship and principal sector are assessed at death on 20 November 2025. No current personal holding is attributed to the deceased after the April 2026 sale.

Namesake risk is substantial: Panos J. / Panagiotis son of Ioannis / Panaras differs from Panos D. / son of Dimitrios / Panoulis. Widely repeated obituaries attach pharmacy/Paris education, Titan and Cycladic Museum details to the deceased; primary Titan identity evidence points to the cousin. Those claims are withheld rather than propagated.

Family succession plus official ultimate ownership supports family transfer, but no deed or probate establishes inheritance. Original retail-sector materiality is an inference from the documented central operating platform, not the first pharmacy established by ancestors. The family group's enterprise totals are never assigned as his personal fortune.

The terminal coffee asset is positively attributed to him by a business obituary, with contemporaneous governance and primary corporate-history corroboration. Its exact cap table, personal liabilities and estate composition are unavailable; the coffee company had non-performing borrowing. No personal net worth, positive net equity or sale-proceeds amount is asserted.

Birth day and month, additional nationality and a firmly supported terminal residence change remain unknown. Birth year and Athens are explicit in the Greek original obituary. Death components are high-confidence candidates only because the immutable baseline marks them inapplicable while Alive; the mortality correction is proposed without rewriting the inventory.

Instagram, LinkedIn and Personal Website were prioritised, followed by Facebook, Twitter/X, Youtube and TikTok with Latin and Greek variants. No personal account was authenticated. LinkedIn Pharmaservice and Marinopoulos Bros name matches lack J./D. disambiguation; the Franklin Templeton/LSE and school-age developer profiles are different generations. ICARUS Sports results concern another Panos and are excluded. Family members' Instagram accounts are not his.

No verified person-relevant Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor or Zillow account was found. No exact personal Wikipedia or Forbes profile was established. Corporate Starbucks/Alshaya sites are research evidence rather than proposed links to a presently owned business.

Only Grocery retail and Coffee industry meet the active taxonomy's defining operations test. Family pharmaceutical interests, occasional publishing investment and unverified cultural roles do not justify extra tags. Private relationships appear only where needed for identity resolution, never as biography colour.
